newsitem.title: UK: TENNIS-IVANISEVIC PICKS UP SPEED AT QUEENS CLUB.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-IVANISEVIC PICKS UP SPEED AT QUEENS CLUB.

text.p: Third seed Goran Ivanisevic brushed aside the challenge of Britain's Martin Lee at Queen's Club on Thursday and then privately focused his sights on the Wimbledon title he so covets.

The Croatian left-hander blitzed world number 500 Lee on an overcast Centre Court 6-1 7-5 to reach the last eight of the 700,000-dollar London Grasscourt Championships, showing the sort of composure that has often been lacking in his previous bids to capture the top prize at Wimbledon.

After a disappointing first-round exit at the French Open, the 25-year-old Ivanisevic came to London nine days ago -- the earliest he has ever arrived in Britain to prepare for the grass Grand Slam event -- and said he thought the decision had been sound.
"I got here early, played a little football and funned around a little...and now my mood is good," said the Croat whose biggest enemy has often been his own temperament.
"For Wimbledon you have to be mentally right, to stay there for two weeks on grass is very tough.
"But I am not going to say anything about my chances at Wimbledon because in the past I have said too much about it and it has not come true."
Ivanisevic faces Frenchman Jerome Golmard in the Queens quarter-finals after the world number 103 triumphed 2-6 6-1 6-4 over compatriot Jean-Philippe Fleurian.
Sixth-seeded Australian Mark Philippoussis blew away Zimbabwean Byron Black 6-3 6-3 and 16th-seeded Briton Greg Rusedski outclassed Australian Scott Draper 6-3 6-2.

Sweden's Jonas Bjorkman, seeded eight, finished off his match from Wednesday night against Mexican Luis Herrera, winning 7-5 7-5, and seventh-seeded American Jim Courier completed a 6-3 6-2 victory over South Africa's David Nainkin.
